title: Two kinds of le, and no past tense
summary: Tell the completion 了 le from the change-of-state 了 le, and stop calling either one past tense.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: The particle 了 le is the most over-explained word in Mandarin, and the usual explanation is wrong: it is not a past tense marker. Mandarin locates a sentence in time with words like 昨天 zuótiān (yesterday) and 以后 yǐhòu (after), and 了 le instead says something about the shape of the situation. Two jobs matter to learners. Verb 了 le sits right after the verb and presents an action as done: 我买了两本书 wǒ mǎi le liǎng běn shū (I bought two books), 他去了三次 tā qù le sān cì (he went three times). It wants an object or a number after it, so a bare 我吃了 wǒ chī le leaves a listener waiting for the rest.

Sentence 了 le sits at the end and flags a new situation or a change: 下雨了 xià yǔ le (it has started raining), 我饿了 wǒ è le (I am hungry now), 他不喜欢这里了 tā bù xǐhuan zhèlǐ le (he no longer likes it here). The two can stack: 我已经吃了饭了 wǒ yǐjīng chī le fàn le (I have already eaten). Habitual sentences take neither: 我七点起床 wǒ qī diǎn qǐchuáng is fine, but 我每天早上起了床 wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang qǐ le chuáng sounds odd. Negation with 没 méi usually pushes 了 le away: 我没吃饭 wǒ méi chī fàn is right, and 我没吃了饭 wǒ méi chī le fàn is not.

blocks.title: Practise these
body: 我看了两个小时的电影。 wǒ kàn le liǎng gè xiǎoshí de diànyǐng. — I watched a film for two hours.
她学了三年中文。 tā xué le sān nián Zhōngwén. — She has studied Chinese for three years.
孩子睡着了。 háizi shuìzháo le. — The child has fallen asleep.
我要一杯咖啡，不要茶了。 wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi, bú yào chá le. — I want a coffee instead of tea now.
他昨天没来上课。 tā zuótiān méi lái shàng kè. — He did not come to class yesterday.
我们下个月去上海。 wǒmen xià gè yuè qù Shànghǎi. — We are going to Shanghai next month.

blocks.body: Independent, unofficial practice material written from scratch for general learners of Mandarin. It teaches the two jobs of the particle le, and nothing in it is taken from, copied from, or aligned to any commercial course, textbook brand, app, or official exam. It is not an answer key for any test.
